这是一个非常简单的 ComfyUI 初学者友好的 Inpaint 工作流程，它将与具有多个 LORA 的单个 QWEN Image GGUF 模型一起使用（此工作流程需要 ComfyUI 的 LORA Manager 插件才能运行。最好安装 ComfyUI 管理器和 LORA Manager 插件，以帮助您轻松下载和管理检查点、LORA 和其他资源。这两个不仅对此工作流程有帮助，而且在任何其他情况下都会为您提供很多帮助）。您需要一个 Hugging Face 帐户来下载必要的 QWEN 图像文件（详细信息如下）。确保使用 ComfyUI 管理器为 ComfyUI 安装 GGUF 插件，并将正确的文件放置在正确的位置。另请查看我的 SD 1.5 + SDXL 1.0、HiDream、WAN 和 通量。

如何使用这个 -

#1.只需先选择您想要的 QWEN Image GGUF 模型，然后加载

#2.从 LORA Manager 启动一个或多个匹配的 LORA

＃3。然后在“加载蒙版图像”上加载您的蒙版图像（如果您想将其与 ComfyUI 的蒙版编辑器一起使用，您也可以在此处加载用于蒙版的原始图像）以编写输出的正面和负面提示。

＃4。选择您想要的图像数量（更改“运行”按钮旁边的数字）

＃5。选择图像采样方法、CFG、步骤等设置

＃6。最后按运行按钮生成。就是这样..

** 您还可以加载原始未屏蔽图像以在可选查看窗格上查看并将其与修复输出进行比较。

享受吧！

o.en:
This is a very simple ComfyUI beginner friendly Inpaint workflow that will work with a single QWEN Image GGUF model with multiple LORAs (This workflow does require ComfyUI's LORA Manager plugin to function. It is a good idea to install both ComfyUI manager and LORA Manager plugin to help you easily download and manage Checkpoints, LORAs and other resources. Not only these two are helpful for this workflow but they will help you a lot in any other cases). You need a Hugging Face account to download your necessary QWEN Image files (Details are mentioned below). Make sure you install GGUF addon for ComfyUI using ComfyUI manager and place the correct files in correct places. Also check out my other workflows for SD 1.5 + SDXL 1.0, HiDream, WAN and Flux.

How to use this -

#1. Just select your desired QWEN Image GGUF model first and then load

#2. one or multiple matching LORA(s) from LORA Manager to start

#3. then load your masked image on "Load Masked Image" (if you want to use it with ComfyUI's Mask Editor you can load your original image for masking here too) to write your positive and negative prompts for output.

#4. select how many images you want (Change the number besides the "Run" button)

#5. select image sampling methods, CFG, steps etc. settings

#6. finally press the run button to generate. That's it..

** You can also load your original unmasked image to view and compare it with inpainted output on an optional viewing pane.

Enjoy!
